discovery_mentions.text: 1. Extract `r1_wire::parse_record` alone first (source lines 39–74). Its direct Rust cone is `row_shape`, `Error::{InvalidRow,Length,Tag,NonCanonical}`, `LANES`, `CLAIMS`, `WideExact::from_le_bytes`, `WideExact::c1`, and `QM31::ZERO`. It also depends on slice length/index/range operations, `try_into().unwrap()` for the fixed 4-byte length field, `chunks_exact(32).enumerate()`, and `Result` propagation. `row_shape` is a small finite match; payload-size arithmetic is `0`, `32`, `28*32`, `(CLAIMS+LANES)*32`, or `LANES*32`.

The cut contains no replacement `unreachable!()` implementation for either the field reader or decoder. Charon followed the field reader into the real, transparent `WideExact::from_le_bytes` and `WideExact::from_limbs` bodies. Aeneas emitted source-backed Lean definitions for all three declarations. The exact extraction output and command/receipt/admission evidence are under `attempt1/`.

This host-only test invokes `WideExact::from_le_bytes` from two actual full field modules: the baseline is the current `field.rs` plus unchanged `wide_exact.rs`; the candidate is the same full `field.rs` plus the isolated `WideExact::from_le_bytes` candidate from `wide-parser-extraction-20261015/input-b`. It compares panic, `None`, and returned eight-limb values and rejects panic outcomes on every vector. Canonical limb vectors must return their exact limbs.

These isolated attempts exercise only the actual `WideExact::from_le_bytes` parser through `crate::parse_wide_exact_probe`. They use complete pinned field sources from worktree revision `aba310f1daa065a27da89d15c6c47166037a8a71`. The repository runtime sources were not edited. Every attempt used the same pinned Charon/Aeneas pair, `--mir built`, `core::option` and `core::result` includes, release/offline Cargo settings, and a `MemoryHigh=4G, MemoryMax=6G, MemorySwapMax=0, TasksMax=128` scope. `--monomorphize` was used in a/b and omitted in c/d to match the prior successful field parser run.

The baseline `WideExact::from_le_bytes` source was tested in a and c. The candidate in b and d changes only that function body to check the 32-byte length and parse two 16-byte `QM31` slices, returning `Some(Self { c0, c1 })`; `from_limbs` is untouched. The exact diff and source pins are retained.

This isolated extraction starts from the original pinned `field.rs` and `field/wide_exact.rs`. The final h2 candidate retains every original `#[inline(always)]` attribute, changes only `WideExact::from_limbs`'s limb-range guard and `WideExact::from_le_bytes`'s parser body, and preserves the destructuring and field-construction code byte-for-byte. The local checker verifies that exact diff.

This isolated candidate changes only `WideExact::from_limbs` and `WideExact::from_le_bytes` in `crates/aspis-core/src/field/wide_exact.rs`. The first uses eight explicit limb-range checks before the unchanged canonical construction. The second checks the input length and constructs eight little-endian `u32` limbs from literal four-byte arrays before calling the unchanged `from_limbs`. The function attributes and surrounding source remain as pinned. `source/wide-unrolled.patch` is the exact source patch; `source/source-manifest.sha256` pins 751 files and the pre/post-build verification logs report zero mismatches.

discovery_mentions.text: This focused packet proves successful-output inversion for the exact Aeneas-generated `fast_domain.fibre_point` body from adopted source revision `c8ea8dd49c81ab970b9dbee8d8b47718f9beb005`. It is deliberately scoped to `fibre_point`; `QueryGeometry::for_range` remains blocked by Aeneas `InterpBorrows` on the real Vec iteration body (the v7 attempt is separately preserved in diagnostics if available).

This packet pins the exact `fast_domain::line_node` and `fibre_point` bodies emitted by the focused Aeneas extraction, and checks the explicit-operations adapter used by the Lean theorem against those bodies. It contains no Lean objects.

The Rust source revision is `c8ea8dd49c81ab970b9dbee8d8b47718f9beb005`. The focused source cut contains the exact copied `fast_domain.rs`, roots `fast_domain::line_node` and its `fibre_point` dependency, and excludes `QueryGeometry`/`for_range`. The exact source SHA is in `metadata/source-pins.json`. Charon and Aeneas both exited 0 under fresh 1 GiB high / 2 GiB max / swap-0 scopes; their receipts and generated source hashes are in `evidence/extraction/`.

`proof-sources/R17FibrePointLineNode.lean` proves the mathematical line-expression / `storedFirstLineX18` relation from the successful retained fibre-point owner. `proof-sources/R17FibrePointLineNodeActual.lean` adds the actual three-step `line_node` monadic sequence with explicit `M31Ops` and a source-compatible fibre-point operation parameterization. `evidence/source-check/check-source-adapter.py` (v6) reverses exactly the recorded substitutions and compares the normalized raw source bodies for `table_value`, `fibre_point`, and `line_node`; it also checks the ordered 512-pair TABLE_A and TABLE_B literals against the exact selected narrow Funs child source `Funs-selected-narrow.lean` (source SHA `ca34b291966b1289d1e50c867e2d7fafc91e7f55a2cb6fdb94461f4968d4ce58`, object SHA `fefca8beeefd8d413083c8499ee7d6b026e2275207a833364a2c2301561fcc17`). The older `Funs-chunked-adapter.lean` is retained only as historical evidence and is not used by the v6 checker. The checker confirms the operation-parameter substitutions for `table_value` and `fibre_point`, plus exact ordered TABLE_A/TABLE_B literal equality after concatenating the 16 chunks in order. The checker result is recorded in `evidence/source-check/result.json`.

This packet does **not** establish that the extracted Rust `Vec` implementation refines the list model. It also does not prove `fibre_point`'s table lookups and CM31 operations equal the stored formal circle point. Those actual-source adapters remain open. The exact `fast_domain.rs` snapshot is included at `source-pins/fast_domain.rs` (SHA256 `bf4b66a59f6a23d19adf6f0021dfa0b9ddb010d6611181d13374fec12c612151`) to pin the relevant implementation.

discovery_mentions.text: Inside semantic parsing, `Prefix::parse` checks that the semantic bytes contain the C1 root, all 27 framed rows, and no trailing bytes (`r1_wire.rs:265–293`). `parse_record` enforces the row's exact tag and `5+payload` length, and for rows 14–26 canonical-decodes every WideExact payload word and rejects nonzero high components (`:38–74`). `SemanticTranscript::new` also converts the serializer-produced public-byte length to `u32` before its first hash (`:173–180`). These checks precede the corresponding hash operations. A proof that is structurally valid but fails a semantic boundary or terminal relation can, however, already have hashed earlier rows before rejection (`r1_semantic.rs:70–125`).

2. Add `ValidatedRecord` and `decode_k` next (lines 112–163). Its cone includes the private `{ row, framed }` token, `parse_record` as the issuance condition, row/offset checks, `checked_mul` / `checked_add`, `payload`, `.get(range)`, `chunks_exact`, and `QM31::from_le_bytes(&part[..16])`. The crucial separation is that `decode_k` itself only checks `row >= 14`; its assurance that each 32-byte value has zero high half comes from the token's construction through `Prefix::parse` calling `parse_record`. A source bridge should preserve that issuer/use relation, rather than prove `decode_k` in isolation and silently grant an unchecked token.

3. Add `Prefix::parse` last (lines 268–292). Its direct cone is `Prefix<'a> { c1_root: &'a [u8;32], records: [&'a [u8];27] }`, `Error`, `row_shape`, and `parse_record`. It checks the initial 32-byte root, takes a fixed prefix, runs a 27-iteration row loop computing each exact framed size, stores borrowed subslices by row, advances an offset, and rejects any trailing bytes. `record` / `payload` / `validated_record` are consumers, not required to parse the prefix itself; include them only when proving the token-use bridge.

The likely hard point is the loop updating a fixed array of borrowed slices while the loop's `framed` value borrows the input. Aeneas must preserve the common input lifetime across the array assignment. This differs from merely extracting a 27-element structural loop over owned values. The minimal preflight after steps 1–2 is an exact extraction of `Prefix::parse` with `row_shape` and `parse_record` as imported extracted declarations, then inspect translation shape before attempting any Lean theorem.

`parse_record`, `ValidatedRecord`, and `Prefix::parse` in the current `r1_wire.rs` are attributed by `git blame` to commit `628054cd494c66dc91e4e01612c70bd164ecf276` (the R1 wire checkpoint); the current file blob is recorded above. The field parser source pins are independently recorded above. The earlier `public_bytes` serializer is in `crates/aspis-statement/src/pool_v1/pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs`, SHA-256 `2bb7db64dc53c8a268e42b0fe46da64ab1afcb03d28bbec2569b2abc30cbc074`, introduced at `a383b9d5d7d904c028310981a24a656872885b0`.

The handwritten `SemanticRecordCodec` / `LiteralSemanticPrefix` models define useful exact byte-model APIs and parser laws, but they are not extracted versions of `r1_wire::parse_record` or `Prefix::parse`. No current declaration was found connecting successful `Prefix::parse` to those Lean readers, nor one connecting the `ValidatedRecord` token to the Lean decoder. A future source bridge should add that correspondence in the order above and keep source extraction, Lean proof, and any Rust/compiler correspondence claim as distinct evidence layers.

discovery_mentions.text: Inside semantic parsing, `Prefix::parse` checks that the semantic bytes contain the C1 root, all 27 framed rows, and no trailing bytes (`r1_wire.rs:265–293`). `parse_record` enforces the row's exact tag and `5+payload` length, and for rows 14–26 canonical-decodes every WideExact payload word and rejects nonzero high components (`:38–74`). `SemanticTranscript::new` also converts the serializer-produced public-byte length to `u32` before its first hash (`:173–180`). These checks precede the corresponding hash operations. A proof that is structurally valid but fails a semantic boundary or terminal relation can, however, already have hashed earlier rows before rejection (`r1_semantic.rs:70–125`).

2. Add `ValidatedRecord` and `decode_k` next (lines 112–163). Its cone includes the private `{ row, framed }` token, `parse_record` as the issuance condition, row/offset checks, `checked_mul` / `checked_add`, `payload`, `.get(range)`, `chunks_exact`, and `QM31::from_le_bytes(&part[..16])`. The crucial separation is that `decode_k` itself only checks `row >= 14`; its assurance that each 32-byte value has zero high half comes from the token's construction through `Prefix::parse` calling `parse_record`. A source bridge should preserve that issuer/use relation, rather than prove `decode_k` in isolation and silently grant an unchecked token.

3. Add `Prefix::parse` last (lines 268–292). Its direct cone is `Prefix<'a> { c1_root: &'a [u8;32], records: [&'a [u8];27] }`, `Error`, `row_shape`, and `parse_record`. It checks the initial 32-byte root, takes a fixed prefix, runs a 27-iteration row loop computing each exact framed size, stores borrowed subslices by row, advances an offset, and rejects any trailing bytes. `record` / `payload` / `validated_record` are consumers, not required to parse the prefix itself; include them only when proving the token-use bridge.

The likely hard point is the loop updating a fixed array of borrowed slices while the loop's `framed` value borrows the input. Aeneas must preserve the common input lifetime across the array assignment. This differs from merely extracting a 27-element structural loop over owned values. The minimal preflight after steps 1–2 is an exact extraction of `Prefix::parse` with `row_shape` and `parse_record` as imported extracted declarations, then inspect translation shape before attempting any Lean theorem.

`parse_record`, `ValidatedRecord`, and `Prefix::parse` in the current `r1_wire.rs` are attributed by `git blame` to commit `628054cd494c66dc91e4e01612c70bd164ecf276` (the R1 wire checkpoint); the current file blob is recorded above. The field parser source pins are independently recorded above. The earlier `public_bytes` serializer is in `crates/aspis-statement/src/pool_v1/pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs`, SHA-256 `2bb7db64dc53c8a268e42b0fe46da64ab1afcb03d28bbec2569b2abc30cbc074`, introduced at `a383b9d5d7d904c028310981a24a656872885b0`.

The public serializer Aeneas attempts are preserved under `evidence/public-serializer-extraction-20261015/` and its c/d follow-ups. Attempts b, c (`-loops-to-rec`), and d (optimized MIR) all fail translation at the borrowed mutable-frontier serialization loop (`lib.rs:239:12–243:9`), with `InterpAbs.merge_abs_conts_aux` / `InterpReduceCollapse.repeat_iter_borrows_merge` in the trace. This history is specific to `public_bytes`'s mutable `Vec`/borrowed frontier pattern and does not itself predict the outcome for `parse_record`.

discovery_mentions.text: Current Rust source also exposes distinct functions: the R1 cost-probe `ordinary_sample` and `gamma_sample` are documented as modulo-ranked WideExact maps ([`sampler.rs:75-91`](../../../../crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/sampler.rs)); the core transcript `challenge_qm31` instead reads little-endian words, masks by `P`, retries a limb when the masked word equals `P`, and returns an error on retry exhaustion ([`transcript.rs:395-431`](../../../../crates/aspis-core/src/transcript.rs)). discovery_mentions.text: That guard is called by `composition_parts` at line 1240. Both composition and terminal evaluators route through it: `terminal_parts` calls `composition_parts` at 1302–1304, and the public `r0::Public::terminal_qm31` calls `terminal_parts` at 2044–2063. The relevant circuit/public-digest equations are also built by `public_digest_lanes` (609–694): each old source-index bit chooses an empty-root or old-frontier binding, all levels are included, and the after-root and carry-frontier node are bound separately. `semantic_packed` includes those lanes (1143–1158), and `composition_parts` evaluates `semantic_packed` (1253–1256). Thus the host precheck and the circuit constraints have related level conditions, but they are distinct code paths.

The separate R1 verifier stage-one path does reach the host guard. In the R1 pool adapter, `stage1` accepts `[3,10]` or `[3,11]`, parses and validates the public statement, then calls `super::first(..., data[1] as usize)` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/r1_pool_adapter.rs:867–935`). `process` dispatches those instruction forms to `stage1` (`:981–993`). `first` maps the transfer/withdrawal statement to `r0::Public` and calls `verifier::tx1` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/lib.rs:23–28`). `tx1` performs strict proof parsing, calls `r1_semantic::verify_observed`, and only after it returns prepares the transcript and processes the first `k` queries (`crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/verifier.rs:342–349`). The semantic verifier calls `public.terminal_qm31` before completing semantic verification (`crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/r1_semantic.rs:111–124`); that method calls `terminal_parts` (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:2044–2063`), which calls `composition_parts` (`:1285–1309`), and `composition_parts` calls `validate_transition` at `:1240`. Therefore the current split's stage one executes the full host-side non-carry comparison before it writes the checkpoint, regardless of whether `k` is 10 or 11.

For the semantic `public_bytes` boundary: its serializer validates each emitted M31 `< P` (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:2002–2040`), but does not itself enforce withdrawal positivity/range or transition validity. The ASF8 ASWP decoder's public validator does enforce `0 < amount < 2^30`; the semantic terminal's own `composition_parts` independently rejects zero or amounts `>= 2^30` and calls `validate_transition` (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:1234–1240`). `validate_transition` checks source pool/domain, `sequence == next_pair_index`, source index `< 2^20`, increment by one, and active/inactive frontier equations (`:180–209`). The Lean `SemanticPublicWire.parsePublic` only enforces canonical M31 decoding and variant/option shape with nonzero withdrawal; it does not model the broader ASF8 envelope, account bindings, amount upper bound, or transition checks. This is the exact scope boundary visible from the inspected definitions, not a conclusion about any refinement theorem.

1. **Withdrawal amount validation is in separate layers.** The Lean `parsePublic` applies `PublicOptionShape.check`, which rejects a withdrawal amount of zero (`PublicOptionShape.lean:19–26`). The Rust byte serializer itself only writes the `Option` flag and, for `Some`, runs the M31 field encoder (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:2026–2029`); it does not reject zero there. The terminal evaluation path rejects both zero and values `>= 2^30` in `composition_parts` (`:1234–1240`), reached by terminal composition (`:1303–1304`, macro wrapper `:1359–1368`). The wire parser's M31 decoder rejects noncanonical field values, but accepts canonical values in `[2^30, P)`; `parsePublic` itself only imposes nonzero, so it accepts some values the terminal validator later rejects. This is a parser-versus-terminal-validation boundary, not a byte-order discrepancy.

2. **Index range versus transition validity.** The Lean carrier uses `Fin (2^64)` (`SemanticPublicWire.lean:23`) and proves the mapped public index is below `2^64` (`:123–127`), matching the source `u64` wire width. It does not impose the pool capacity or transition checks. Rust `validate_transition` checks snapshot sequence/index equality, index capacity, increment by one, and frontier cells (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:180–208`), and `composition_parts` invokes it (`:1240`). `parsePublic` is therefore only a wire/option-shape decoder, not a full accepted-terminal validator.

The composition path calls `validate_transition` (180–208), `state_only_poseidon::evaluate_state_only_poseidon_oracle_projected` (589 onward), and copy-terminal selector/evaluation code. The generated candidate has transparent structured bodies for these functions. `composition_parts` also has two generated recursive loops. discovery_mentions.text: That guard is called by `composition_parts` at line 1240. Both composition and terminal evaluators route through it: `terminal_parts` calls `composition_parts` at 1302–1304, and the public `r0::Public::terminal_qm31` calls `terminal_parts` at 2044–2063. The relevant circuit/public-digest equations are also built by `public_digest_lanes` (609–694): each old source-index bit chooses an empty-root or old-frontier binding, all levels are included, and the after-root and carry-frontier node are bound separately. `semantic_packed` includes those lanes (1143–1158), and `composition_parts` evaluates `semantic_packed` (1253–1256). Thus the host precheck and the circuit constraints have related level conditions, but they are distinct code paths.

Source path: `r0::Public::terminal_qm31` (pair forest file 2065–2084) calls `terminal_parts` (1285–1310); that calls `composition_parts` (1216–1283) and `equality_value`. The composition path calls `validate_transition` (180–208), `state_only_poseidon::evaluate_state_only_poseidon_oracle_projected` (589 onward), and copy-terminal selector/evaluation code. The generated candidate has transparent structured bodies for these functions. `composition_parts` also has two generated recursive loops. The emitted external axioms do not themselves provide their intended Rust semantics.

It sets `index = source.next_pair_index` and `carry = min(index.trailing_ones(), 20)`. For each level 0–19, it skips only `level == carry && carry < 20`; otherwise expected after-frontier is the frozen empty root if `level < carry` or the source-index bit is zero, and the old source frontier entry otherwise.

It does not compare active one-bit frontier entries against the old lane frontier. Statement validation is performed by `validate_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` in `crates/aspis-statement/src/pool_v1/pair_forest_terminal.rs:227–276`, which checks public/account bindings and delegates late-transition encoding; the late-statement encoder/decoder checks only the index increment (`pair_tree_profile.rs:529–559`, `634–638`), while afterstate transport validation checks index range and canonical digest limbs (`pair_terminal.rs:113–151`). The Pool program’s zero-bit frontier check is therefore the direct program-side shape guard visible at the persistence boundary; it should not be described as implementing every equality in host `validate_transition`.

discovery_mentions.text: - `decode_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` parses an 1880-byte ASF8 envelope (`pair_forest_terminal.rs:29–41,386–415`, SHA-256 `becc01f162f23cd9b4a7fd3780be5a441c9b7265f3078282244cc938da63a16c`), dispatching to the lane-transition and ASCP/ASWP decoders. The file’s module header (`:1–5`) marks the terminal format inactive for the production `aspis-pool` path. That header does not describe the separate experimental R1 cost-probe acceptance path: `programs/r1-cost-probe/src/lib.rs::first` directly calls this decoder at line 25, converts the result to `r0::Public`, and calls `verifier::tx1` at lines 26–27 (SHA-256 `294546036e6cf8bb8dcc1f1f4a65c5e0887ac04593cdda801f58c75a284d582a`). With the `pool-adapter` feature, `r1_pool_adapter::stage1` accepts `[3,10]` or `[3,11]`, validates the statement, and reaches `super::first` at `r1_pool_adapter.rs:867–935` (SHA-256 `b2adab8610189a5031fc6f28a7cdeef12c01aa292423743cb4696aa3ee1590a4`). Therefore ASF8/ASCP/ASWP parsing is an actual acceptance surface of the experimental R1 verifier, while the production-inactive module comment remains accurate for the mainline Pool route. This inventory does not claim that the experimental path is deployed or prove byte-to-Lean refinement.

The top-level `decode_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` (`pair_forest_terminal.rs:386–415`) requires exactly 1880 bytes, ASF8 magic, the supported terminal version, a recognized transfer/withdrawal kind, and the supported digest-encoding version. It decodes the common block and nested 1520-byte late statement, chooses ASCP or ASWP from the outer kind, then calls `validate_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` before returning. The statement validator (`:227–276`) additionally requires nonzero master/checkpoint/selected-lane account keys and an output lane below the lane count; validates the chosen payment record; binds payment pool to master, payment deployment domain to the late snapshot domain, late snapshot pool to master, payment anchor sequence to checkpoint sequence, payment anchor root to the historical global anchor, and output lane to the nullifier-derived lane; and re-encodes the late statement to exercise its validators.

The full host-side `validate_accounts` path is separate from the ASF8 parser (`pair_forest_terminal.rs:671–734`, called by the host verifier at `:736–742`). It validates master/checkpoint/lane account encodings; binds master account and identity pool, deployment domain, and asset; binds checkpoint account/master/sequence/global root; binds selected-lane account/master/id and initialized-lane bit; requires the runtime withdrawal-destination account to be zero for transfers or equal to the ASWP destination for withdrawals; and compares snapshot sequence/index/root/frontier against the selected lane's live tree. The returned-result validator (`:539–559`) separately binds transition kind, accounts, output lane, nullifier, and verified afterstate to the statement. These host/account bindings should not be attributed to `decode_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` alone.

discovery_mentions.text: The separate R1 verifier stage-one path does reach the host guard. In the R1 pool adapter, `stage1` accepts `[3,10]` or `[3,11]`, parses and validates the public statement, then calls `super::first(..., data[1] as usize)` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/r1_pool_adapter.rs:867–935`). `process` dispatches those instruction forms to `stage1` (`:981–993`). `first` maps the transfer/withdrawal statement to `r0::Public` and calls `verifier::tx1` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/lib.rs:23–28`). `tx1` performs strict proof parsing, calls `r1_semantic::verify_observed`, and only after it returns prepares the transcript and processes the first `k` queries (`crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/verifier.rs:342–349`). The semantic verifier calls `public.terminal_qm31` before completing semantic verification (`crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/r1_semantic.rs:111–124`); that method calls `terminal_parts` (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:2044–2063`), which calls `composition_parts` (`:1285–1309`), and `composition_parts` calls `validate_transition` at `:1240`. Therefore the current split's stage one executes the full host-side non-carry comparison before it writes the checkpoint, regardless of whether `k` is 10 or 11.

discovery_mentions.text: matter to every later oracle input. `stage1`'s final mutable account borrow/copy

| `stage1` | `∀ program accounts data, native1 program accounts data = AdapterRw.r1_pool_adapter.owned.stage1_owned O program accounts data`. All well-typed Lean arguments, including arbitrary account counts/contents/flags/keys, malformed instructions and rejected inputs. No admission or accepted-run restriction. |

`S2W_D189Wrappers.first` reserves snapshots, calls `native1 program e.first data`, propagates rejection, and on success copies the checkpoint into account 2 under the separate std law, releases its guard, then cleans up allocation. `second` reserves snapshots, calls `native2 program (e.second secondSizes) data slot`, propagates rejection and cleans up, returning `e.heap`. These are distinct non-extracted wrapper interpretations. A contract only about real AccountInfo `stage1`/`stage2` acceptance cannot prove the unrestricted owned-function fields: the wrappers supply only selected snapshots and hide the returned checkpoint behind a copy.

These are specification schemas for future Kani contracts, not compiled Rust annotations or certificates. Use actual frozen `programs/r1-cost-probe/src/r1_pool_adapter_owned.rs::{stage1_owned,stage2_owned}` (TX1/TX2 owned entries), not newly written lookalikes. The public AccountInfo `stage1`/`stage2` additionally require the existing snapshot/copy/allocator/wrapper gates. Digest is `SolanaDigest::digest` in `programs/r1-cost-probe/src/lib.rs:13`, whose body is `hashv(parts).to_bytes()`.

This isolated candidate used a source-only patch replacing `try_into().ok()?` with explicit `match` handling in `CM31::from_le_bytes`. The runtime source was not changed. The recorded input source revision is `6e25cda9d35e52df0980dbcd6744522bd3caaab0`; candidate `field.rs` SHA-256 is `28df5a1abee13bde4b3aa9eeceb0489bedf00531f298460954a97661f5f1baea`.

Charon and Aeneas both exited 0. Translation retained four local functions (`M31::from_le_bytes`, `CM31::from_le_bytes`, `QM31::from_le_bytes`, and `parse_fields_probe`), three types, and the `P` global. It also retained bodies for the two non-local Option try helpers. `translation.json` reports `is_opaque: false` for all six functions; the generated Funs file has no external-template declarations. The standalone raw generated files were not compiled directly in this extraction layout. The corresponding retained declarations with pinned Option support are covered by seven green Lean targets in the sibling `lean-candidate-field-parsers-20261014` bundle. These results do not establish Rust compiler correspondence or caller-level parser behavior.

This host-only test invokes `WideExact::from_le_bytes` from two actual full field modules: the baseline is the current `field.rs` plus unchanged `wide_exact.rs`; the candidate is the same full `field.rs` plus the isolated `WideExact::from_le_bytes` candidate from `wide-parser-extraction-20261015/input-b`. It compares panic, `None`, and returned eight-limb values and rejects panic outcomes on every vector. Canonical limb vectors must return their exact limbs.

These isolated attempts exercise only the actual `WideExact::from_le_bytes` parser through `crate::parse_wide_exact_probe`. They use complete pinned field sources from worktree revision `aba310f1daa065a27da89d15c6c47166037a8a71`. The repository runtime sources were not edited. Every attempt used the same pinned Charon/Aeneas pair, `--mir built`, `core::option` and `core::result` includes, release/offline Cargo settings, and a `MemoryHigh=4G, MemoryMax=6G, MemorySwapMax=0, TasksMax=128` scope. `--monomorphize` was used in a/b and omitted in c/d to match the prior successful field parser run.

The baseline `WideExact::from_le_bytes` source was tested in a and c. The candidate in b and d changes only that function body to check the 32-byte length and parse two 16-byte `QM31` slices, returning `Some(Self { c0, c1 })`; `from_limbs` is untouched. The exact diff and source pins are retained.

This isolated extraction starts from the original pinned `field.rs` and `field/wide_exact.rs`. The final h2 candidate retains every original `#[inline(always)]` attribute, changes only `WideExact::from_limbs`'s limb-range guard and `WideExact::from_le_bytes`'s parser body, and preserves the destructuring and field-construction code byte-for-byte. The second checks the input length and constructs eight little-endian `u32` limbs from literal four-byte arrays before calling the unchanged `from_limbs`. The function attributes and surrounding source remain as pinned. `source/wide-unrolled.patch` is the exact source patch; `source/source-manifest.sha256` pins 751 files and the pre/post-build verification logs report zero mismatches.

discovery_mentions.text: The R1 probe adapter has an analogous statement-binding path, but it is a separate executable: `reconstruct_asq8_statement` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/r1_pool_adapter.rs:778–805`) checks old-index plus one equals candidate index, constructs the statement from the authenticated live snapshot and candidate afterstate, and calls transfer/withdrawal statement boxing; those helpers call `validate_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` (751–775). Its ASQA scanner canonical-decodes the supplied candidate bytes (688–729); `stage1` revalidates the statement before copying the candidate into the proof account (867–897). This adapter validation binds the statement and its index, while the full transition constraints are evaluated by the selected verifier.

It does not compare active one-bit frontier entries against the old lane frontier. Statement validation is performed by `validate_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` in `crates/aspis-statement/src/pool_v1/pair_forest_terminal.rs:227–276`, which checks public/account bindings and delegates late-transition encoding; the late-statement encoder/decoder checks only the index increment (`pair_tree_profile.rs:529–559`, `634–638`), while afterstate transport validation checks index range and canonical digest limbs (`pair_terminal.rs:113–151`). The Pool program’s zero-bit frontier check is therefore the direct program-side shape guard visible at the persistence boundary; it should not be described as implementing every equality in host `validate_transition`.

The top-level `decode_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` (`pair_forest_terminal.rs:386–415`) requires exactly 1880 bytes, ASF8 magic, the supported terminal version, a recognized transfer/withdrawal kind, and the supported digest-encoding version. It decodes the common block and nested 1520-byte late statement, chooses ASCP or ASWP from the outer kind, then calls `validate_pool_v1_pair_forest_terminal_statement_v1` before returning. The statement validator (`:227–276`) additionally requires nonzero master/checkpoint/selected-lane account keys and an output lane below the lane count; validates the chosen payment record; binds payment pool to master, payment deployment domain to the late snapshot domain, late snapshot pool to master, payment anchor sequence to checkpoint sequence, payment anchor root to the historical global anchor, and output lane to the nullifier-derived lane; and re-encodes the late statement to exercise its validators.

discovery_mentions.text: The separate R1 verifier stage-one path does reach the host guard. In the R1 pool adapter, `stage1` accepts `[3,10]` or `[3,11]`, parses and validates the public statement, then calls `super::first(..., data[1] as usize)` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/r1_pool_adapter.rs:867–935`). `process` dispatches those instruction forms to `stage1` (`:981–993`). `first` maps the transfer/withdrawal statement to `r0::Public` and calls `verifier::tx1` (`programs/r1-cost-probe/src/lib.rs:23–28`). `tx1` performs strict proof parsing, calls `r1_semantic::verify_observed`, and only after it returns prepares the transcript and processes the first `k` queries (`crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/verifier.rs:342–349`). The semantic verifier calls `public.terminal_qm31` before completing semantic verification (`crates/aspis-r1-cost-probe/src/r1_semantic.rs:111–124`); that method calls `terminal_parts` (`pair_forest_semantic_terminal.rs:2044–2063`), which calls `composition_parts` (`:1285–1309`), and `composition_parts` calls `validate_transition` at `:1240`. Therefore the current split's stage one executes the full host-side non-carry comparison before it writes the checkpoint, regardless of whether `k` is 10 or 11.

These are specification schemas for future Kani contracts, not compiled Rust annotations or certificates.
